title: TikTok as a Source of Oral Hygiene Education: Alignment and Misinformation Relative to Official Dental Guidelines
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 246 Spanish-language TikTok oral-hygiene videos scored against official dental protocols; 73.81% were classified as containing unsupported or non-aligned information, a share of items with a stated denominator. Coded as QUALITY rather than CONTENT (see notes): the label is guideline non-concordance, not a truth/falsity judgement, and a wholly true video can receive it.

estimates.country: not specified for most videos (59% no identifiable country of origin; Mexico the most frequent identifiable origin at 9%); Spanish-language content, study run from Ecuador
estimates.measure_type: % of Spanish-language TikTok oral-hygiene videos containing unsupported or non-aligned information relative to official dental protocols
estimates.value_raw: Overall, 26.19% aligned with at least one protocol, while 73.81% contained unsupported or non-aligned information
estimates.denominator: 246 publicly available Spanish-language TikTok videos on oral hygiene/toothbrushing, collected May-July 2025 via 11 hashtags, after eligibility filtering and duplicate removal
estimates.definition: Video classified as NOT containing aligned information, i.e. not a single evaluated recommendation matched an official oral hygiene protocol (FDI, ADA, FOE/Ecuador Ministry of Health, FDE). The complement, 'aligned', required only ONE matching recommendation.
estimates.misinfo_def: No explicit definition of misinformation is given; misinformation is operationalised as non-alignment with official dental protocols: "Videos were operationally classified as containing 'aligned information' when at least one evaluated recommendation aligned with an official oral hygiene protocol."
estimates.source_quote: As results, only 1% of videos cited official references. Overall, 26.19% aligned with at least one protocol, while 73.81% contained unsupported or non-aligned information.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract; Results section 3.3 "Accuracy of Oral Hygiene Information"; Discussion p. 7
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Standardized evaluation summary derived from FDI, ADA, Federacion Odontologica Ecuatoriana (with Ecuador's Ministry of Public Health) and Federacion Dental Espanola guidelines, covering toothbrush characteristics, technique, toothpaste, mouthwash, floss and electric toothbrush features. Two calibrated evaluators independently assessed all videos on a structured form; triple-blinded (blind to each other's ratings and to engagement metrics); discrepancies resolved by a third reviewer. Cohen's kappa = 0.86 on a pilot calibration sample.
estimates.moderator_quote: Videos were operationally classified as containing "aligned information" when at least one evaluated recommendation aligned with an official oral hygiene protocol. This binary classification was used for comparative statistical analyses at the video level. ... Videos categorized as containing "aligned information" could also include incomplete, unsupported, or non-aligned recommendations in other evaluated domains. ... the dichotomous categorization may have introduced misclassification bias by oversimplifying the multidimensional nature of informational quality.
estimates.notes: CONSTRUCT CALL (the main thing for an adjudicator to check). Coded QUALITY, not CONTENT, and flagged borderline. The paper does call the variable 'accuracy' and its title says 'Misinformation', which pulls toward CONTENT via the 'guideline concordance stated as accurate/inaccurate' clause. But the operational label is guideline NON-CONCORDANCE, and the non-aligned category is described as 'unsupported OR non-aligned' - i.e. it absorbs claims that are simply not covered by a protocol. A wholly true video that gives sound advice not matching a protocol item, or that covers no evaluated variable, lands in the 73.81%, which is exactly the instruction's 'wholly true item could receive the label' test for QUALITY. The authors reinforce this: floss type 'could not be established... due to the absence of protocol guidance', and they concede the binary rule 'may have introduced misclassification bias'. Two further biases push the estimate: (a) the aligned category needed only ONE matching recommendation, inflating the non-aligned share for videos of narrow scope; (b) the eligibility criteria EXCLUDED videos 'promoted home remedies or pseudotherapies', removing the most misinformation-laden content and biasing the estimate DOWNWARD in the opposite direction. Corpus is 11 hashtags of algorithm-ranked TikTok results from a fresh account, hence denom_selection=curated.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Per-component non-alignment shares were NOT entered as separate rows (all are the same measure on sub-denominators of videos mentioning that component; entering them would inflate and would mix denominators): toothbrush bristles 55 videos (22.36%) of which 78.18% (n=43) aligned; toothbrush handles not protocol-based in 98.18% (n=54); toothbrush heads not protocol-based in 80% (n=44); technique addressed in 17 videos (6.91%), brushing movement 100% (n=17) protocol-based, angulation 70.59% (n=12) aligned, frequency and time not protocol-based in 82.35% (n=14 each); toothpaste in 53 videos (21.54%), fluoride presence not protocol-based 90.57% (n=48), fluoride concentration 98.11% (n=52), toothpaste quantity 66.04% (n=35); mouthwash in 62 videos (25.20%), components 96.77% (n=60), instructions 85.48% (n=53); floss in 99 videos (40.24%), instructions 70.71% (n=70), frequency 86.87% (n=86); electric toothbrush in 20 videos (8.13%), movement 60% (n=12) aligned. Each is an exact part/whole share and could be recovered if component-level rows are wanted. (2) "only 1% of videos cited official references" (two videos) is a citation-practice measure, not misinformation prevalence. (3) Engagement statistics (mean 0.46 million views, mean ~900 likes, max 24.9 million views) are attention intensities, not misinformation exposure, so no per_capita_intensity row; the reported like-count 'differences' of 211,121.22 and 21,583.66 are inconsistent with a stated mean of ~900 likes and a maximum of 0.01 million, an apparent reporting error worth flagging. (4) All chi-square associations in Table 1 are tests, not prevalence. (5) The eligibility criteria excluded videos promoting home remedies or pseudotherapies - an exclusion that removes likely-misinformation content from the denominator and should be recorded as a downward bias on the 73.81%.

rob.design: Observational, analytical, cross-sectional content analysis. Publicly available Spanish-language TikTok videos on oral hygiene collected May-July 2025 through 11 hashtags, using a newly created account with no viewing history to reduce personalization bias; final sample 246 videos after exclusions (home remedies/pseudotherapies, product marketing without educational content, orthodontic/periodontal/child/animal-specific content, no technique demonstrated, duplicates). Evaluation instrument: standardized summary of FDI, ADA, FOE/Ecuador MoH and FDE recommendations across toothbrush, technique, toothpaste, mouthwash, floss and electric toothbrush variables. Two calibrated evaluators rated all videos independently under a triple-blinded procedure, third reviewer adjudicated discrepancies; Cohen's kappa = 0.86 on a pilot sample. Chi-square, Z-tests for proportions and Mann-Whitney U in SPSS 30.1, alpha 5%. No IRB required (public content). Authors' stated limitations: Spanish-language and hashtag-restricted sampling, algorithm-driven variability in hashtag yield, and the oversimplifying binary aligned/non-aligned classification. ChatGPT (GPT-5.3) was used for grammar and writing clarity per the Acknowledgments; coding is described as human.
rob.item6_quote: Videos were operationally classified as containing "aligned information" when at least one evaluated recommendation aligned with an official oral hygiene protocol.
rob.item10_quote: Considering all evaluated variables based on the selected protocols, 26.19% of the analyzed videos contained information aligned with at least one official recommendation.
